rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī takes the making level as bringing Adam to balance and full readiness to receive the spirit.
rows.anchor: فعلت فيه ما يصير به مستويا معتدلا مستعدا لفيضان الروح

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative explanation is that God formed Adam in human shape and the human constitution.
rows.anchor: وقيل : صورته بالصور الإنسانية والخلقة البشرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ordinary usage, blowing means sending air from the mouth or elsewhere into a cavity able to hold and fill with it.
rows.anchor: النفخ في العرف إجراء الريح من الفم أو غيره في تجويف جسم صالح لإمساكها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here blowing figuratively represents imparting actual life to receptive matter; no literal blowing occurs.
rows.anchor: والمراد هنا تمثيل إفاضة ما به الحياة بالفعل على المادة القابلة لها وليس هناك نفخ حقيقة

rows.speaker: حجة الإسلام
rows.claim: Al-Ghazālī explains the blowing image as a cause standing for its effect: prepared clay is like a wick ignited by fire, though the resulting life need not resemble the cause.
rows.anchor: وقال حجة الإسلام : عبر بالنفخ الذي يكون سببا لاشتعال فتيلة القابل من الطين

rows.speaker: حجة الإسلام وجماعة من المحققين
rows.claim: Al-Ghazālī and other verificationists describe the spirit as an immaterial substance, neither body nor bodily accident, and neither inside nor outside the body or joined to it or separate from it.
rows.anchor: ثم هذا الروح عنده وكذا عند جماعة من المحققين ليس بجسم يحل البدن

rows.speaker: جماعة من المحققين
rows.claim: Their first proof says universal intelligible forms cannot inhere in a point, which would always be receptive and make every point-bearing body rational, or in divisible matter, which would divide the forms.
rows.anchor: وكذا عند جماعة من المحققين ليس بجسم يحل البدن

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Sheikh's self-knowledge proof says self-awareness cannot depend on a second equal image, which duplicates the self; direct presence to oneself instead implies a self-subsisting, nonbodily intellect.
rows.anchor: والدليل الثاني : ما عول عليه الشيخ وزعم أنه أجل ما عنده في هذا الباب

rows.speaker: أفلاطون
rows.claim: Plato argues that the mind can distinguish imagined nonexistent forms; the small body cannot contain these vast forms, and surrounding air is neither part of the body nor an instrument of the soul.
rows.anchor: أفلاطون وهو أنا نتخيل صورا لا وجود لها في الخارج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth proof argues that if perceptions inhered in a body, one part could know while another part was ignorant of the same thing at the same time.
rows.anchor: الدليل الرابع : لو كان محل الإدراكات شيئا جسمانيا لصح أن يقوم ببعض ذلك الجسم علم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fifth proof rejects an embodied soul: it would always perceive its organ, never perceive it, or perceive it only sometimes; each fails, and an image of the organ would either duplicate itself or require an immaterial soul.
rows.anchor: الدليل الخامس : أن الروح لو كان منطبعا في جسم مثل قلب أو دماغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the Imam's al-Mabāḥith presents twelve proofs, including arguments already given, then relies on a further argument.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر الإمام في المباحث من الأدلة اثني عشر دليلا

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam's favored argument starts from our self-evident awareness that we are the same person as before: the self is neither the changing body nor an accident dependent on it, so it is an immaterial substance.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر الإمام في المباحث من الأدلة اثني عشر دليلا

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: He adds that animals may know their own identities, but do not know that their present selves are those that existed earlier, so the immaterial human self need not belong to every animal.
rows.anchor: ولا يلزم أن يكون لسائر الحيوانات هذا الجوهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī introduces another proof: one entity in a person is the perceiver for every kind of perception and every object perceived.
rows.anchor: قد دللنا على أن المدرك بجميع أصناف الإدراكات لجميع المدركات شيء واحد في نفس الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unified perceiver cannot be the body itself, a quality in every body part, or a quality in just one part: we do not find every part perceiving or one all-purpose perceiving organ.
rows.anchor: فلو كان بعض الأجسام سواء كان جزأ من البدن أو محصورا في جزء منه موصوفا بالقوة المتعلقة بجميع هذه المدركات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nor can the perceiver be a subtle body hidden in an organ, since no such location is experienced; because we directly know ourselves as perceivers, an unknown body's identity cannot explain that self-awareness.
rows.anchor: إنا قد دللنا على أنا السامعون المبصرون المتخيلون العاقلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These arguments conclude that the common subject of perception is neither body nor body-dependent, but an immaterial substance.
rows.anchor: فثبت أن الموصوف بالقوة المدركة لجميع المدركات ليس جسما أصلا ولا قائما به

rows.speaker: الذاهبون إلى التجرد
rows.claim: Those who hold the spirit immaterial say its bond with the body resembles an instinctive, divinely inspired lover's attachment to the beloved and governs and directs the body while it remains receptive.
rows.anchor: وذكر هؤلاء الذاهبون إلى التجرد أنه متعلق بالبدن كتعلق العاشق عشقا جبليا إلهاميا بالمعشوق

rows.speaker: حجة الإسلام
rows.claim: Al-Ghazālī says the possessive attribution 'My spirit' reflects creation without an intermediary that serves as origin or matter, or serves as an honorific attribution.
rows.anchor: وإضافته إلى ضميره تعالى في الآية لأنه سبحانه وتعالى خلقه من غير واسطة

rows.speaker: حجة الإسلام
rows.claim: Al-Ghazālī compares this attribution to the sun saying it gave earth its light: the light is of the sun's kind, though extremely weak by comparison; the spirit's spacelessness and universal knowledge mark a likeness that warrants the attribution.
rows.anchor: لو نطقت الشمس وقالت : أفضت على الأرض من نوري يكون ذلك صدقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī answers that two spaceless beings can remain distinct through their essences, just as different qualities in one body, or the same quality at different times, are distinct without separate places.
rows.anchor: التميز غير منحصر بالمكان بل يكون به لجمسمين في مكانين وبالزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the objection that being outside place is uniquely divine: God's unique attribute is self-subsistence, while everything else depends on and borrows its existence from Him.
rows.anchor: وكون الوجود لا في مكان أخص صفاته سبحانه في حيز المنع بل الأخص أنه جل شأنه قيوم

rows.speaker: المناوي
rows.claim: Al-Munāwī says the factions' many rational speculations on the spirit yielded no sure result; Ibn Jamāʿa held that none of the more than a thousand views is sound.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ عبد الرؤف المناوي : قد خاض سائر الفرق غمرة الكلام في الروح فما ظفروا بطائل

rows.speaker: جمهور أهل السنة
rows.claim: The Sunni majority instead holds that the spirit is a subtle body differing from other bodies in essence and qualities, dwelling in the body like oil in olives or fire in coal; al-Juwaynī adopts this view.
rows.anchor: وجمهور أهل السنة على أنها جسم لطيف يخالف الأجسام بالماهية والصفة

rows.speaker: اللقاني
rows.claim: Al-Laqqānī describes the spirit as a luminous, self-living, subtle upper body permeating the organs like rosewater in a rose; it does not decay, and its presence is life while separation is death.
rows.anchor: وقال اللقاني : جمهور المتكلمين على أنها جسم مخالف بالماهية للجسم الذي تتولد منه الأعضاء

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some identify the human being with the visible bodily frame and make the spirit an accident inhering in it.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن الإنسان هو هذا الهيكل المحسوس وروحه عرض قائم به

rows.speaker: بعض المتأخرين من المعاصرين
rows.claim: Some later contemporaries ascribed that view to the majority of theologians and used it, together with the impossibility of uniting prior states, to argue that a servant does not create his own acts.
rows.anchor: وعراه بعض المتأخرين من المعاصرين إلى جمهور المتكلمين وجعله وامتناع اتحاد القبل دليلا

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam rejects identifying the person with the visible frame and approves the majority position, since bodily parts continually change while the person remains the same from beginning to end.
rows.anchor: رد الإمام في التفسير ذلك الزعم وارتضى ما نقلنا عن الجمهور

rows.speaker: جمهور المتكلمين
rows.claim: The majority reason that the enduring self cannot be the body, whose parts continually wither, grow, increase, diminish, mature, and dissolve; what changes completely is not the persistent person.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز أن يكون الإنسان عبارة عن هذا الهيكل المحسوس لأن أجزاءه أبدا في الذبول والنمو والزيادة والنقصان

rows.speaker: المحققون
rows.claim: Among accounts of the self, the most satisfactory concise one says it consists of bodily components pervading the frame like water in a rose or oil in sesame; the discerning add that these components differ in nature from the frame's changing parts.
rows.anchor: أن أسدها تحصيلا وتلخيصا أنها أجزاء جسمانية سارية في هذا الهيكل سريان الماء في الورد والدهن في السمسم

rows.speaker: المحققون
rows.claim: On this bodily-soul account, its own persistent particles are luminous and alive; they animate the changing frame, then separate at its corruption for the realm of holiness if blessed or afflictions if wretched.
rows.anchor: ثم إن المحققين منهم قالوا أن الأجسام التي هي باقية من أول العمر إلى آخره

rows.speaker: صاحب الهياكل
rows.claim: The author of al-Hayākil argues that we never lose awareness of ourselves although we sometimes forget body parts; since a whole is known only through its parts, the self is beyond the body.
rows.anchor: كلام صاحب الهياكل حسبما يدل عليه كلام شارحه الجلال حيث قال في الهيكل الثاني

rows.speaker: الجلال
rows.claim: Al-Jalāl objects that this proves only that the soul is beyond the visible body, not that it is immaterial; it could still be a subtle body.
rows.anchor: وقال الجلال : فلا تكون النفس جسما أصلا لأن غاية ذلك إثبات أن النفس وراء هذا البدن

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī says most theologians regard the spirit as an accident identical with life; Ustadh Abū Isḥāq adopts this despite the resulting accident-in-an-accident problem.
rows.anchor: وزعم القاضي أن مذهب أكثر المتكلمين أن الروح عرض وأنها هي الحياة واختاره الأستاذ أبو إسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī answers that a spirit's being bodily does not make every body a spirit: it is spirit through a special divine property and is alive in itself, so no infinite regress of spirits follows.
rows.anchor: فإنه إنما كان روحا لمعنى خصه الله تعالى به وقد علمت أن القائل بالجسمية يقول : إنه حي لذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The animal spirit is a subtle vaporous body generated from subtle humors, arising from the heart's left cavity and spreading through the body as the rational soul's vehicle of control.
rows.anchor: وعرفه في الهياكل بأنه جسم لطيف بخاري يتولد من لطائف الأخلاط وينبعث من التجويف الأيسر من القلب

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another account identifies the spirit with the balanced temperament of the heart's blood.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إنه اعتدال مزاج دم القلب

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: Some verificationists distinguish a subtle spirit permeating the body from a noble divine-command spirit that shines upon it and may give it life, perception, and luminosity.
rows.anchor: وذهب بعض المحققين إلى أن الروح تطلق على الروح التي ذكر أنها جسم لطيف سار في البدن

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: They take the spirit meant by the question in 17:85 to be the second, divine-command spirit.
rows.anchor: ويعبر عنه بالروح الأمري وهو المراد من الروح في قوله تعالى : ( يسألونك عن الروح ) الآية

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: In this terminology, the first spirit is the human self, while the second is the rational self; the immaterial substance described as neither body nor bodily is the spirit in this latter sense.
rows.anchor: ويطلقون كثيرا على الروح بالمعنى الأول النفس الإنسانية وعليها بالمعنى الثاني النفس الناطقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars disagree whether souls originate before or after bodies.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا في أن حدوثها هل هو قبل الأبدان أو بعدها

rows.speaker: حجة الإسلام
rows.claim: Al-Ghazālī holds that souls arise when bodies become ready to receive them, like an image appearing when a mirror is polished, although the image's source existed earlier; Aristotle and his followers also held this.
rows.anchor: فقال حجة الإسلام : الحق أن الأرواح حدثت عند استعداد الجسد للقبول كما حدثت الصورة في المرآة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection cites a report that God created spirits two thousand years before bodies; no chain or grading is supplied here.
rows.anchor: خبر أن الله تعالى خلق الأرواح قبل الأجسام بألفي عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī reports Ghazālī's answer that the spirits in this report are angels and the bodies are the world's vast bodies, such as the Throne, Kursī, and heavens, rather than human bodies.
rows.anchor: لعل المراد من الأرواح في الخبر الأول الملائكة عليهم السلام وبالأجساد أجساد العالم من العرش والكرسي والسماوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument likens human spirits to a lamp kindled from an immense fire covering the world, the last spirit among the angels, and human bodies to the vastly larger cosmic bodies.
rows.anchor: ولو انفتح عليك باب معرفة أرواح الملائكة لرأيت الأرواح البشرية كسراج اقتبس من نار عظيمة

rows.speaker: حجة الإسلام
rows.claim: His argument against preexistent souls says one soul shared by all would make everyone share the same knowledge and ignorance, while dividing one immaterial soul into many is impossible.
rows.anchor: بأنها لو كانت موجودة قبل الأبدان فإما أن تكون واحدة أو كثيرة وعلى الأول إما أن تتكثر

rows.speaker: حجة الإسلام
rows.claim: If preexistent souls were already many, their individuation would require differences in essence, necessary properties, or accidents; shared species rules out the first two, while accidents cannot precede the body that supplies matter.
rows.anchor: وعلى الثاني لابد أن يمتاز كل واحدة منها عن صاحبتها إما بالماهية أو لوازمها أو عوارضها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه الصلاة والسلام
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying presents Muhammad as the first prophet in creation.
rows.anchor: وأما قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : أنا أول الأنبياء خلقا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه الصلاة والسلام
rows.claim: Another Prophetic saying says Muhammad was a prophet while Adam was between water and clay.
rows.anchor: وقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : كنت نبيا وآدم بين الماء والطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation reads “created” in the first-prophet report as predestination, not actual existence: ends precede their means in design but follow them in existence.
rows.anchor: فالخلق فيه بمعنى التقدير دون الإيجاد فإنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قبل أن يولد لم يكن مخلوقا موجودا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The architect's completed house is first as a design and last to exist; preparatory work serves it, just as first thought is last in the finished work.
rows.anchor: فالدار الكاملة أول الأشياء في حق المهندس مثلا تقديرا وآخرها وجودا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human creation aims at knowing the happiness of nearness to God, attainable only through prophetic instruction; prophethood's completion in Muhammad is the goal, making him first in the plan and last in historical existence.
rows.anchor: ولما كان المقصود من فطرة الآدميين إدراكهم لسعادة القرب من الحضرة الإلهية ولم يمكنهم ذلك إلا بتعريف الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report about Adam is taken to indicate that Adam was made to yield the purest descendant, with selection continuing through generations until Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وأنه لم يشأ سبحانه خلق آدم إلا لينتزع الصافي من ذريته ولم يزل يستصفي تدريجا إلى أن بلغ كمال الصفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion distinguishes an ideal existence in the planner's mind from external existence; God's prior decree is inscribed on the Preserved Tablet before realization, as an architect's design precedes a house.
rows.anchor: أن للدار مثلا وجودين وجودا في ذهن المهندس حتى كأنه ينظر إلى صورتها ووجودا خارج الذهن مسببا عن الوجود الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine Pen conveys forms to the receptive Tablet according to eternal knowledge; neither need be physical, and they may be understood as spiritual teacher and learner.
rows.anchor: واللوح عبارة عن موجود قابل لنقش الصور والقلم عبارة عن موجود منه تفيض الصور على اللوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Pen and Tablet analogy is linked to 96:4, “He taught by the pen,” and the passage concludes that Muhammad preceded others in ideal existence, not actual existence.
rows.anchor: بقوله سبحانه : ( علم بالقلم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first objection to the prior-soul proof asks why one preexistent soul could not later multiply; the reply distinguishes connected divisible unity from unity in general, since a universal affirmative does not convert.
rows.anchor: الأول لم لا يجوز أن يقال : إنها كانت قبل الأبدان واحدة ثم تكثرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second objection asks why multiple preexistent souls need distinct attributes: if attributes distinguish things, each attribute also needs distinguishing, producing circularity or infinite regress.
rows.anchor: الثاني سلمنا أنها كانت متكثرة لكن لم قلتم لابد أن يختص كل بصفة مميزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third objection says souls might differ by essential properties; the proof that they share one species does not establish that they must.
rows.anchor: الثالث سلمنا أنه لابد من مميز فلم لا يجوز أن يكون بذاتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth objection allows preexistent souls to differ through accidents caused by matter, proposing that each might have been attached to an earlier body, and so on; excluding this requires disproving transmigration.
rows.anchor: الرابع سلمنا أنها لا تتميز بشيء من الذاتيات فلم لا يجوز أن تتميز بالعوارض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion says Ghazālī's proof of the soul's origination then depends on refuting transmigration, while philosophers use origination to reject it; the proposed chain leads to two souls in one body and circularity.
rows.anchor: ولا مخلص من هذا إلا بإبطال التناسح فتوقف حجة إثبات حدوث الأرواح على ذلك الإبطال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fifth objection asks why, even without any previous body, souls could not differ by accidents, each caused by an earlier accident without a first one.
rows.anchor: الخامس سلمنا عدم تعلقنا ببدن قبل لكن لم لا يجوز أن تكون موصوفة بعارض باعتباره كانت متميزة
